description: The figure presents three pie charts comparing the distribution of four outcome categories across difficulty levels labeled “easy,” “medium,” and “hard,” with a total of 4 slices per pie and a shared legend on the right. In the “easy” chart, the slices are N+K+ (teal) at about 40.6%, N−K+ (yellow) at about 45.9%, N−K− (light orange) at about 10.1%, and N+K− (red-orange) at about 3.3%, with percentage labels shown inside each slice. In the “medium” chart, N+K+ (teal) is about 44.6%, N−K+ (yellow) about 44.3%, N−K− (light orange) about 7.2%, and N+K− (red-orange) about 3.9%, again with internal percentage labels. In the “hard” chart, N+K+ (teal) is about 20.1%, N−K+ (yellow) about 36.2%, N−K− (light orange) about 36.8%, and N+K− (red-orange) about 7.0%, with percentages labeled inside the slices. No slices appear exploded or offset, and while the slice ordering varies by chart, the legend consistently maps colors to the four labels.
